system: AMP (Agent Messaging Protocol) relay — Fareground agent-messaging, PyPI fg-amp
version: fg-amp 0.12.1 from PyPI (release commit a26c517; installed sources byte-identical to repo HEAD fd2d6ae21878dabe5b17a26e689f55f4033e6054, whose later commits are docs only); fg-agent-id 0.2.0; wire protocol amp/0.1
language: Python 3.12.12 (FastAPI 0.142 + uvicorn 0.54 with uvloop/httptools; cryptography 50.0.2 provides Ed25519, X25519, ML-KEM-768, ChaCha20-Poly1305)
driver_notes: Run it once per concurrency level against a freshly launched relay, and sample the relay PID yourself (same method as silk-bench foreign). Optional flags: --warmup (default 100), --rt-samples (default 300), --rt-warmup (default 10 untimed roundtrip samples, as silk-bench), --audience (default amp-bench; must equal the relay's --audience), --timeout (default 120 s per wait), --no-uvloop. Pass --relay ws://127.0.0.1:{PORT} for the WebSocket push transport instead of HTTP long-poll. Prints one JSON object on stdout (progress on stderr). 'level' has the same keys and percentile method as silk-bench throughputLevel (concurrency, requests, seconds, msgs_per_sec, p50_ms, p90_ms, p99_ms, errors). 'roundtrip_pct' matches silk-bench pct (samples, p50, p90, p99, mean) and measures send -> recipient session.receive() -> recipient relay ack completed. Also reported: roundtrip_detail_ms (send, send_to_receive, send_to_relay_ack, send_to_sender_receipt), send_throughput.delivered_msgs_per_sec, handshake_ms, and client.sender_cpu_util_timed / receiver_cpu_util_timed (near 1.0 means the Python client, not the relay, is the bottleneck). Valid concurrency 1..256. It spawns one child process (the receiver endpoint), which exits with the driver. Smoke-tested (19 messages each) over HTTP against the SQLite and in-memory relays and over WS against the SQLite relay.
launch_notes: Single OS process: uvicorn runs one worker in the launched PID (no forking, no child processes), so sample that PID's RSS/CPU. With --db, SQLite I/O runs on asyncio.to_thread pool threads inside the same PID. relay_launch.py only rebinds three module globals and then calls the unmodified fg_amp.transport.relay.main(): _RATE_MAX_REQUESTS 240 -> 1e6 per signed source per 60 s on send/pull/ack/ws-auth (at the stock value the benchmark gets HTTP 429 after 240 sends per minute from one sender), _MAX_PER_SENDER 512 -> 1e6 and _MAX_MAILBOX_SIZE 4096 -> 1e6 undelivered envelopes (HTTP 507 when a lagging receiver lets the backlog grow). Run with cwd={DATADIR}; it writes nothing except the --db file. uvicorn's default INFO access log writes one line per request to stdout: redirect stdout/stderr to a file. SHUTDOWN: on SIGTERM uvicorn waits for in-flight requests, and an outstanding long-poll pull can hold the process for up to about 30 s ('Waiting for background tasks to complete'; observed). Send SIGKILL after a short grace period if the harness needs the port back quickly.
health_notes: There is no health endpoint. GET /amp/v0/relay/cards (card-directory delta listing, unauthenticated, cheap) returns 200 {"cards":[],"cursor":0} as soon as uvicorn accepts connections. Observed cold start to the first 200 was 0.35-0.55 s with warm .pyc and about 2 s on the first launch after install.

per_worker_setup.how: fg_amp.AgentIdentity.generate(name) for X (sender) and Y (receiver): an Ed25519 signing key plus an X25519 agreement key. Address = 'amp:key:' + base58(ed25519 public key).

Y = AmpNode(identity, policy=ContactPolicy(mode=OPEN, rate_limit_per_peer>=C, max_sessions>=256), on_session=cb). The stock open policy admits only 10 initiations/min/peer. Y runs in a separate process.

RelayTransport(base_url, audience='amp-bench').connect(node) for each node, one transport per node (sharing one transport short-circuits delivery in-process). HTTP: PUT /amp/v0/relay/cards with the self-signed card, then a background long-poll loop: POST /amp/v0/relay/pull {address, ts, sig, wait_seconds:25}. WS (ws:// URL): the same PUT, then GET /amp/v0/relay/ws upgrade with a signed auth frame.

X: session = await X.initiate(y_card): a sealed handshake.initiate envelope (X25519 + ML-KEM-768 hybrid) goes through the relay to Y's mailbox. Y's policy accepts and returns handshake.accept through the relay. Each session costs about 4 relay requests plus 2 acks. Session.send holds a per-session lock across the relay POST, so concurrency C needs C sessions (one closed-loop worker per session).

body.body: <base64(32-byte ratchet DH public || ChaCha20-Poly1305 ciphertext of JSON {content_type:'text/plain', content:TEXT, metadata:{}})>
body.sig: <base64 Ed25519 over signing_input('envelope', envelope minus sig)>

wire.response: 200 {"accepted": true, "id": "<envelope id>"}; 422 bad envelope or signature; 429 rate limit; 507 mailbox quota

send.relay_work: read body (1 MiB cap), check canonical JSON, pydantic parse, Ed25519 verify, rate-limit check. In-memory: deque append. --db: 2x SELECT COUNT(*) + INSERT + COMMIT (fsync). Then wake long-poll waiters.

receive.api: message = await session.receive() on Y (the session arrives through on_session)

body.sig: <base64 Ed25519 over signing_input('relay-pull', {action:'pull', address, audience, ts}); single-use>

wire.response: 200 {"envelopes": [<wire envelopes>]}. It blocks up to wait_seconds (capped at 30) until mail arrives. Every pending envelope is leased (moved to in-flight for 30 s), not deleted.

receive.client_work: Y verifies the envelope signature, then (per envelope) a DH ratchet step on direction turns, HKDF chain step, AEAD decrypt, payload screen, and a RECEIPT envelope {rseq, ack, missing, window} signed by Y and POSTed to /amp/v0/relay/send for X. So each message causes 2 relay sends.

ack.api: automatic: after the handler returns, Y's RelayTransport poll loop acks the handled envelope ids (bench.py observes the outcome and does not change it)

body.sig: <base64 Ed25519 over signing_input('relay-ack', {action:'ack', address, audience, ids, ts})>

ack.e2e_ack: Y's RECEIPT envelope is the protocol's end-to-end delivery ack. X processes it after its own pull, and that pull is relay-acked too.
ack.ws_variant: Over WS, sends are {type:'send', envelope} frames answered by {type:'sent'}. Deliveries are pushed as {type:'deliver', envelopes}. Acks are {type:'ack', ids} frames (no per-ack signature: the socket was authenticated once with a 'relay-ws' signature) answered by {type:'acked'}.

signing_input: uint16be(len(tag)) || tag || canonical_json(payload), tag = UTF-8('fg-amp/v1/' + context). canonical_json is json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False) + NFC, with floats rejected.
relay_requests_per_message: HTTP mode, steady state: X send, Y pull, Y receipt send, Y ack, X pull (the receipt), X ack = 6 relay requests and (with --db) 6 SQLite commits per application message. Pulls and acks are batched when several envelopes are pending.
install_notes: site-packages = 41.6 MB after use, of which 6.9 MB is .pyc generated at runtime (about 34.6 MB excluding .pyc). Installed with uv pip install 'fg-amp[http]==0.12.1' (33 packages) into a uv venv on the uv-managed CPython 3.12.12 (/Users/nrav/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.12-macos-aarch64-none), which is excluded.
notes: STORAGE: in-memory by default (dicts and deques; lost on restart). With --db, SqliteRelayState stores mailbox, in-flight leases, cards, revocations and key revocations in one SQLite file. It uses Python sqlite3 defaults: journal_mode=DELETE (rollback journal, not WAL) and synchronous=FULL, one shared connection serialized by a threading.Lock, and a commit per enqueue, drain and ack. On macOS SQLite's fsync is plain fsync(), not F_FULLFSYNC (fullfsync is off), so a commit is not a guaranteed platter flush there. The spec launches with --db to match a durable SQLite design. Long-poll waiters are in memory either way. DELIVERY: at-least-once. Pulled envelopes are leased for 30 s and redelivered if not acked; after 12 attempts they are dead-lettered. The sender's session also retransmits unacked frames every 5 s (RTO) until Y's receipt arrives. ENCRYPTION: end to end. The handshake is sealed to the recipient's X25519 prekey, with an ML-KEM-768 hybrid contributing to the root (pq_hybrid_handshake=true was negotiated in the smoke runs, but ML-KEM runs only at handshake and resume, never per message). Per message there is a double ratchet (X25519 DH step on each direction turn, HKDF chain otherwise) and ChaCha20-Poly1305. Every envelope is Ed25519-signed and verified by the relay on send and by the recipient. Routing metadata (from, to, session_id, seq, type, created_at) is cleartext to the relay, and receipt bodies are signed plaintext JSON. TRANSPORT: plain HTTP or WS on localhost, no TLS. AUTH: no bearer tokens or accounts. Sends authenticate by envelope signature, pulls and acks by a fresh audience-bound Ed25519 signature (120 s freshness, pull signatures single-use), and the WS socket by one signed auth frame per 300 s. Cards are self-signed. The relay holds no ledger and no transcript; transcripts and hash chains live only at the endpoints. Unmodified limits still active: 1 MiB envelope cap, 30 s lease, 12 delivery attempts, 120 s pull freshness, ContactPolicy max_sessions 256, and the 256-frame reorder window and 512-frame send buffer per session.
